accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE English programmes of study, English Appendix 2, Year 5 (linking ideas across paragraphs using adverbials of time, place and number, e.g. later, nearby, secondly), the upper key stage 2 writing composition statement on building cohesion within and across paragraphs (Eng.UKS2.Write.Comp.2d, the code on this topic), the KS2 GPS test framework glossary definition of an adverbial and of a fronted adverbial taking a comma, and Common Core W.4.3c and W.5.3c on transitional words and phrases. Every opener in the sorter, timeline, map, report and Then-fix rounds was rechecked: Meanwhile is time (same time), Firstly, Secondly and In addition are number, Beyond the river and Nearby are place.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented Year 5 and 6 slips: reading Meanwhile as later (timeline prediction, the R2 and R3 Meanwhile feedback, challenge tag later), choosing an adverbial that clashes with the content (The next morning when owls hoot, Across the river for bats in a cave), ordering report points by guesswork (In addition placed second, Finally placed early), overusing Then (Not just Then prediction 'Then is bad grammar', challenge tag wrong), story links in reports (Secondly in the story draft, challenge tag story) and comma placement inside or splitting the fronted adverbial (challenge tags comma and split).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagadvl models the job of a paragraph opener: a time adverbial moves a reader pin along a four-slot story timeline, a place adverbial flies a reader ring across a story map, number adverbials fix the order of a four-paragraph report, and each vague Then opener is swapped using a time or place clue. flagcohe works within one paragraph (pronoun and synonym reference chains, sentence-level conjunctive adverbials) and flagfront covers the comma after fronted adverbials inside a sentence; neither moves a reader through time or space. The 30% shingle gate passed against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each rule by its effect: choosing Later that night for the brother 'still lost in the forest' moves the pin to night and is rejected with the clue, Meanwhile keeps the pin at noon and is accepted; Across the river flies the ring to the river and is rejected for bats; the report only builds as Firstly, Secondly, In addition, Finally; Secondly is refused in the story draft. Done messages then state the rule (Time adverbials move the clock, Place adverbials move the camera).

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'later on' for Meanwhile, 'when' for Across the river, 'In addition' straight after Firstly, and 'Then is bad grammar'. Each task straight after makes the learner act against the wrong pick, and A.reveal quotes their guess in the done message.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with tagged wrong answers and their own corrections: time and num (Moments later moves the clock, In addition adds a point), later and last (Meanwhile is the same time; Finally is the last point), story and first (story links versus report order), wrong and cant (Then is not wrong but tells nothing; paragraphs often open with an adverbial), comma and split (comma straight after the whole fronted adverbial). In-lab taps also name the slip with the paragraph's own clue.

readability.evidence: Learner kid text scores 4.8 against the learner kid limit of 6.5 with short sentences and real openers (Adverbials of place move the camera: Beyond the river, Back at the castle). Adult text scores 8.5 against 9.5 while using the exact curriculum terms adverbial, fronted adverbial, cohesion, cohesive device, adverbials of time, place and number, English Appendix 2 Year 5 and W.5.3c.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed. Each kid paragraph carries one idea (why openers matter, time and Meanwhile, place and number, matching plus Then and the comma); adult paragraphs give the curriculum statements, the definition and how each type links, five named mistakes and the lab outline. Overlap with Cohesion within paragraphs, Fronted adverbials and Narrative writing stays under the 12% gate.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px Android (light) and iPhone 13 (dark) screenshots for all six steps: paragraph cards wrap onto two lines, the four option tiles sit in a 2 by 2 grid at least 40 px tall, the timeline labels (morning, noon, night, next day) and the map labels stay clear of the reader marker, the four report paragraphs fit the stage, and the challenge canvas text is split onto three lines so nothing clips.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, no console or page errors, and all five Show me tasks completed. Every drag or tap has a labelled button twin ('Adverbial of time', 'Start with Meanwhile', 'Next paragraph: Firstly, a garden…', 'Replace Then with The next morning') and the canvas aria-label speaks each result, e.g. 'Later that night puts the reader at night. But "still lost" means at the same time.'
